s1.syndrome_frame: Acute chest pain with electrocardiographic and laboratory evidence of myocardial injury, complicated by hypotension
salient_findings: Sudden-onset chest pain with increasing intensity
ST-segment elevation in multiple leads on ECG
Elevation of high-sensitive troponin T level
Thrombotic occlusion of the distal left circumflex artery on emergency angiography
key_facts: The patient is an older woman
The patient has a history of diabetes
The patient has a history of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation
The patient presented with sudden-onset chest pain
The intensity of pain increased over time
Initial vital signs showed a normal heart rate and blood pressure
Blood pressure later fell to 60/40 mm Hg
ECG showed ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF
ECG showed subtle ST-segment elevation in leads V7-V9
ECG showed downward-sloping ST-segment depression in leads V2-V4
High-sensitive troponin T level was elevated at 0.309 ng/mL
Emergency angiography showed thrombotic occlusion of the distal left circumflex artery
Computer tomography angiography revealed contrast present in the myocardium and pericardial effusion

shortlist.label: Acute myocardial infarction
shortlist.why_kept: ECG findings of ST-segment elevation and elevated troponin T level

shortlist.label: ST-elevation myocardial infarction
shortlist.why_kept: ECG findings of ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF

shortlist.why_kept: Hypotension with blood pressure falling to 60/40 mm Hg

shortlist.label: Cardiac tamponade
shortlist.why_kept: Pericardial effusion revealed by computer tomography angiography

shortlist.why_kept: Emergency angiography showed thrombotic occlusion of the distal left circumflex artery

shortlist.label: Prinzmetal's angina
shortlist.why_kept: Sudden-onset chest pain and ST-segment elevation

shortlist.label: Coronary artery dissection

shortlist.why_kept: Sudden-onset chest pain and elevated troponin T level without coronary artery disease

raw.rationale: The patient's ECG showed ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF, and subtle ST-segment elevation in leads V7-V9, which is consistent with an ST-elevation myocardial infarction. Additionally, the elevated high-sensitive troponin T level and emergency angiography showing thrombotic occlusion of the distal left circumflex artery support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Acute myocardial infarction
rejected.why: While the patient did have a myocardial infarction, the specific type is better described as ST-elevation myocardial infarction due to the ECG findings.

rejected.label: Cardiogenic shock
rejected.why: The patient's low blood pressure is consistent with cardiogenic shock, but it is a consequence of the myocardial infarction rather than the primary diagnosis.

rejected.label: Cardiac tamponade
rejected.why: There is no clear evidence of cardiac tamponade, such as equalization of diastolic pressures or a large pericardial effusion causing hemodynamic compromise.

rejected.label: Coronary artery thrombosis
rejected.why: While the patient did have a coronary artery thrombosis, this is a component of the ST-elevation myocardial infarction rather than a separate diagnosis.

rejected.label: Prinzmetal's angina
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and ECG findings are not consistent with Prinzmetal's angina, which typically involves transient ST-segment elevation without myocardial infarction.

rejected.label: Coronary artery dissection
rejected.why: There is no clear evidence of coronary artery dissection, and the emergency angiography showed thrombotic occlusion rather than dissection.

rejected.label: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: The patient's ECG findings and elevated troponin level are not consistent with Takotsubo cardiomyopathy, which typically involves a distinctive ballooning pattern on echocardiography and minimal troponin elevation.
